Anchors before first contact (decided 2026-10-10), all three must agree:
(a) the Web PKI certificate of the join point's domain;

(b) DNSSEC validated INSIDE the client from an embedded trust anchor (the donor installs nothing): TXT _swarma.<domain> = root fingerprint, SSHFP = our SSH host key, TXT _swarma-ssh-ca = the host CA, TLSA = the join point's TLS key;

(c) the invitation's pins when an invitation exists: root fingerprint, SSH host key fingerprint, join point certificate, one-use random code (>= 128 bits), delivered through whatever channel the donor found us by.
Proof of possession: the transcript signed over a SERVER challenge (not a client nonce).
No human second channel, no voice comparison. No step downgrades on failure.
POST /join/challenge {invitation_id}
invitation known, unexpired, not consumed? attempt counter
server_challenge (5 min)
TXT _swarma, SSHFP, TXT _swarma-ssh-ca, TLSA (+ RRSIG chain)
records and signatures
validate DNSSEC locally from the embedded trust anchor;
secure: must equal the invitation's pins; bogus or indeterminate: refuse
transcript = canonical CBOR, domain-separated:
{version, invitation_id, project, role, K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh, server_challenge, client_nonce, expires_at, algorithms}
HTTPS validated by the Web PKI, pinned by the DNSSEC-validated TLSA (and the invitation's certificate fingerprint when present)
POST /join/cert {transcript, sig_K_sig(transcript), code}
code equal (constant time)? signature valid? challenge bound and fresh?
consume the invitation atomically -> tombstone(invitation_id, K_sig)
(same K_sig retry -> same pending enrolment; other key -> refuse); rate limit
show {invitation_id, fingerprint, name, role}
check the enrolment against the signed marketplace card when there is one,
otherwise the invitation the code binds; no voice comparison
pin K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh; root-signed admission; grants (scope, expiry)
package: AEAD to K_enc with AAD = H(transcript); signed by the operator certificate (root-signed, scope onboard)
release package for <invitation_id>
POST /join/challenge {invitation_id} (second challenge)
POST /join/collect {invitation_id, sig_K_sig(second challenge)}
package
decrypt with K_enc; verify operator cert chain to the pinned root;
verify package signature; check AAD; pin our SSH host key and host CA from the package
AND cross-check against the invitation and the DNSSEC-validated records
Pinned afterwards:
on our side K_sig, K_enc, K_ssh in the registry and K_ssh in the root-owned authorized-keys file of the workplace user;
on the donor side our root, the operator certificate, our SSH host key, the binding digest, the qualified tuple, the policy generation.
Every later message: signed over exact bytes by K_sig on the donor, fresh, replay-checked, grant-checked (ADM).
Replay: cert/collect meet the tombstone; frames meet connection-scoped ids and op_key caches.
SSH afterwards: host certificates from the host CA (@cert-authority); the worker's K_ssh in a short user-CA certificate (about a day, principal = the workplace user), renewed over the channel.
Rotation: our host key -> new SSHFP + "init --rotate-host" with a fresh invitation; operator cert -> root-signed record; K -> revoke + new enrolment.
